SUBJECT:  ORDINANCE 09-693 - CORRECTION

The Issue

Shall the City Council introduce Ordinance 09-693 – Correction, to correct a typographical error in
the original adopted ordinance referencing the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code (PVEMC)
Chapter – “Taxicabs”?

Analysis and Findings

In September 2009, the City Council considered a staff report and Ordinance to repeal certain
obsolete chapters of the PVEMC, including the chapter titled “Taxicabs”. In that staff report and
ordinance, references throughout to “Taxicabs” were shown as Chapter 5.16, rather than the correct
Chapter – 5.12.

As soon as staff became aware of the error, we consulted with the City Attorney, who prepared the
attached correcting ordinance. The ordinance is self-explanatory and documents the history and
intent of the repeal. The reference to “Taxicabs” as Chapter 5.16 is considered a scrivener’s error.
The correcting ordinance references the intended Chapter 5.12 as being repealed. All other
references within the original Ordinance 09-693 remain intact. The correcting ordinance will be
filed with the original ordinance to document this action.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council introduce Ordinance 09-693 – Correction, which provides
the correct reference to the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code Chapter 5.12 – “Taxicabs” as
being repealed.

Should the City Council award a construction contract for the completion of the FY 10/11 Overlay

Background and Analysis

As part of the annual Capital Improvement Program, various streets receive an overlay treatment.
The work consists of removing and replacing deteriorated asphalt, edge grinding, and overlaying the
surface with new asphalt. The purpose of the work is to prevent any further deterioration of the
roadway and restore the road to its original condition.

In April of 1996, the City Council approved a Pavement Management System report that
inventoried the conditions of all the City streets. The PMS was updated in 2003 and streets were
ranked and prioritized based on their conditions and need for repair. Using the rankings designated
for each street as well as recent field observations, staff identified the following streets for this

SUBJECT:  SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR THE MALAGA COVE LIBRARY TO

  SATURDAY, AUGUST 28, 2010.

DATE:  JULY 13, 2010

ISSUE

Shall the City Council approve a Special Event Application for the Palos Verdes Library District to
hold Sing-A-Long Event featuring the movie Mary Poppins at Farnham Martin Park on Saturday,
August 28, 2010 from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. including set-up and tear-down?

BACKGROUND AND ANALYSIS

The PV Library District would like to hold its second annual sing-a-long event at Malaga Cove
Library on the grounds of Farnham Martin Park. This family event would include playing the movie
Mary Poppins on a screen at the park. Attendees would be encouraged to sing along with the songs
with seating on the grass (no chairs) similar to the Malaga Cove Concert Series. The event would
start with a small program of songs and a costume contest with the 139-minute movie beginning at
8 p.m. The library plans to remain open during the event to provide restrooms and staffing.

Last year, the Library had a similar event featuring the Sound of Music. The attached letter from the
Malaga Cove Library Branch Manager describes the positive feedback received from patrons of last
year’s sing-a-long event. Although the event ran longer than proposed, there were no complaints
reported to the City.

Library representatives have prepared a comprehensive Special Event Application. The Application
has been reviewed and preliminarily approved by all municipal departments. As is consistent with last
year, it is recommended that all fees be waived since the Library District is a public agency. The City
has received a Certificate of Insurance and Indemnity Agreement and notice will be provided to
residents within the area affected.

ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO COUNCIL

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
JULY 13, 2010
  14
 1.  The Council may choose to approve the request of Palos Verdes Library District’s Malaga
  Cove Branch to hold a Mary Poppins Sing-A-Long event at Farnham Martin Park on Saturday,
  August 28, 2010.

2.  The Council may modify or impose further requirements on the Palos Verdes Library
  District.

3.  The Council may decline to approve the Special Event Application as presented.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council approve the request of Palos Verdes Library District’s Malaga
Cove Branch to hold a Sing-A-Long event at Farnham Martin Park on Saturday, August 28, 2010.

SUBJECT:  REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE PALOS VERDES STABLE FY
  2010-11 OPERATING BUDGET

The Issue

Should the City Council approve the Palos Verdes Stable FY 2010-11 Operating Budget?

Background and Analysis

HGS Management Company, LLC has operated as the Concessionaire of the Palos Verdes Stable
since March 1, 2009. The purpose of this report is to share with the City Council a status report on
the FY 2009-10 Budget and to present the proposed FY 2010-11 Stable Operating Budget for
review and approval.

Attachment A to this report includes FY 2009-10 Budget information and the Proposed Stable
Budget for FY 2010-11. Overall, HGS Management is ending 2009-10 with a net profit of $70,352
– adjusted downward from the original projected profit of $92,185 for FY 2009-10. There are a
number of factors which together have contributed to the positive budget performance over the past
year including: (1) The renting of many previously vacant stalls at the stables, (2) a significant
increase in revenue from training activity at the Stable in comparison to prior years, (3) additional
revenues derived from charging for supplemental services including premium hay, turnout services,
and the like, and (4) controlling expenditures and achieving operational efficiencies which will
continue into future years.

For FY 2010-11, HGS is not proposing to increase either the boarding fees or the service fees
charged at the Stable. Attachment B includes a copy of Resolution 2009-03 which set the
maximum fees the concessionaire may charge. Again, there are no proposed changes in this fee
structure for FY 2010-11.

For the coming fiscal year, given the very high level of stable occupancy, boarding revenue will be
at an all time high of $420,000. This amount is $32,288 greater than the projected year end board
revenue for FY 2009-10. Additionally, revenues derived from trainer activity at the stable will
result in $60,000 in FY 2010-11 which is a slight increase over FY 2009-10.

In terms of expenditures, the Proposed FY 2010-11 Budget reflects the experience gained from
HGS’ first full year of operation. There are certain expenditures that are significantly less costly

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
JULY 13, 2010
  16
 than originally projected when HGS began operating the Stable. The most notable areas where
savings have been experienced include the cost of hay and shavings.

Additionally, repair and maintenances costs at the stables are budgeted at $24,000 which is
comparable to what was spent in FY 2009-10 by HGS. In FY 2009-10, HGS completed some much
needed improvements including painting, fence repairs, and new footing in the arenas. For FY
2010-11, HGS will further enhance the Stable with improvements to the hay barn, additional repair/
replacement of fencing, and other necessary work. Lastly, the cost for removal of manure was
higher than originally assumed at the onset of the concession agreement. The proposed budget
allocates $26,400 for manure removal which is nearly double the $14,000 originally projected for
this work.

The Stable will generate a profit of $83,190 in FY 2010-11 after satisfying all obligations under the
concession agreement including payment of the 5% concession fee to the City. The concession
payment totals $25,312 for FY 2010-11.

The boarding statistics for the Stable are included as Attachment C to this report. All stalls at the
Stable are occupied with a total of 72 horses on site. Attachment D to this report is a seven year
budget history of the Stable operation covering the time prior to arrival of HGS Management LLC
as the Stable Operator. A review of this budget history helps demonstrate how HGS has been able
to enhance the revenue generating capacity of the Stable while simultaneously controlling operating
expenditures.

On June 28, 2010, the Stable Liaison Committee (Mayor Pro Tempore Rea and Councilmember
Perkins) met with City Manager Hoefgen and Stable Operators David McLewee and Erin Isom-
McLewee. Following a review of the budget materials and discussion of past year’s Stable
operations, the Council Liaisons recommend Council approved of the Proposed 2010-11 Palos
Verdes Stable Budget.

Looking ahead to the next six month period, the McLewee’s will develop a list of capital
improvement projects at the Palos Verdes Stable with review City Staff and the Council Liaisons.
In addition, the City and HGS will jointly fund a financial audit of the Palos Verdes Stable
operations.

Alternatives Available to Council

The following alternatives are available to the City Council:

  1. Approve the Palos Verdes Stable FY 2010-11 Operating Budget.
  2. Approve the Palos Verdes Stable FY 2010-11 Operating Budget with Modifications.
  3. Decline to act.

Recommendation from Staff
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
JULY 13, 2010
  17
 It is recommended that the City Council review and approve the Palos Verdes Stable FY 2010-11
Operating Budget.

The Issue

Should the City Council send a letter to Los Angeles County 4th District Supervisor Knabe’s office
in support of the development of a dog park on a portion of the former Palos Verdes Landfill
Property?

Background and Analysis

The former Palos Verdes Landfill site consists of 175 acres of land owned by Los Angeles County
located in the in the city limits of Rolling Hills Estates. As City Councilmembers are aware, there
has been considerable interest on the part of dog enthusiasts who have advocated for the placement
of a “dog park” on a portion of the former landfill property.

On June 22, 2010, the City of Rolling Hills Estates sent to 4th District Supervisor Knabe the
attached letter stating that a small portion of the site would be able to support the needs of dog
owners from around the South Bay, and expressing the Rolling Hills Estates’ City Council’s support
for the development of a dog park on the former Palos Verdes Landfill. A copy of the June 22nd
letter is included as Attachment A to this report.

The lead proponents of the proposed dog park at the former landfill site have been Mr. Bruce and
Mrs. Maureen Megowan of Palos Verdes Estates. Attachment B to this report is a copy of an eight
page dog park proposal which Mr. and Mrs. Megowan recently presented to the RHE Parks and
Activities Commission and to the Rolling Hills Estates City Council.

Given that the City of Rolling Hills Estates is now advocating for the use of a small portion of the
former landfill site as a dog park, it is appropriate for the City of Palos Verdes Estates to express its
position on this subject to the County of Los Angeles. Attachment C to this report is a draft letter
for City Council consideration in this regard.

Alternatives Available to Council

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
JULY 13, 2010
  19
 The following alternatives are available to the City Council:

  1. Send a letter to Los Angeles County 4th District Supervisor Knabe’s office in support of the
  development of a dog park on a portion of the former Palos Verdes Landfill Property.

  2. Send a modified letter.

  3. Decline to send a letter.

Recommendation from Staff

It is recommended that the City Council send a letter to Los Angeles County 4th District Supervisor
Knabe’s office in support of the development of a dog park on a portion of the former Palos Verdes
Landfill Property.

TO:  JOSEPH M. HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  JUDY SMITH, ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  PALOS VERDES ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE
  REVIEW AND RECODIFICATION

The Issue

Shall the City Council review, provide input and approve the proposed parameters for the review
and recodification of the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code (PVEMC).

Background

The last codification of the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code (1988) took place more than 20
years ago. Although there have been numerous approved changes to the Code in the intervening
years, reflected as supplements, both the Council and staff wish to undertake a review and
recodification of the PVEMC.

This project has been included in prior years’ work programs, but was not completed in a
comprehensive manner due to workload and staffing issues. Four obsolete sections of the code were
eliminated in the fall of 2009 and the City Clerk’s Office retained our code publishing vendor to
conduct an overview of the code as a first step in the process. The review, completed in December
2009, will provide information useful to the City Attorney and staff.

Analysis and Findings

It is anticipated this will be a very time consuming and labor intensive project. In order to proceed
in an orderly and timely fashion, staff recommends as a first step that the Council review, provide
input and approve the proposed parameters for the code review.

It is the intent of the recodification project to accomplish the following:
  • Update the Code, including statutory references, to reflect current state and federal law;
  • Eliminate vague, ambiguous and overly broad language;
  • Correct/update code provisions which are inconsistent with current practice; and
  • Correct internal inconsistencies within the Code.

It is not the intent of the project to review and revise the policies under which the City currently
operates. For example, under Title 6 – Animals – consideration of cat licensing or mandatory
spay/neuter requirements would not be introduced in the context of other required revisions to these
chapters. Similarly, as an example, Section 1.20.010 regarding General Municipal Election will be
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
JULY 13, 2010
  21
 modified to delete reference to the prior April even-year election, but discussion of election
consolidation or alternate to the March odd-year election date would not be part of the this review.

Policy issues will be addressed to the extent they arise in the context of bringing the code into
compliance with state or federal law. The Council recently revised Chapter 9.05 “Picketing Private
Residences” and considered several policy issues (e.g. distance from property, duration of
picketing). The City Attorney will be well versed to advise the Council in these situations. Policy
may also be addressed in the context of providing direction to staff if internal inconsistencies in the
code involve inconsistent policy, though staff is not immediately aware of any items that fall into
this category.

Based upon Council’s approval of the project parameters as outlined above, staff will then be able
to more firmly develop a timetable, process and estimate of associated City Attorney time and cost
for the project. Staff will bring a follow-up report to the Council at the next meeting.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council review, provide input and approve the proposed parameters
for the review and recodification of the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code.

SUBJECT:  PRESENTATION OF FY 2010-11 WORK PROGRAM

Issue

Presentation of the FY 2010-11 Work Program for the City of Palos Verdes Estates

Background and Analysis

Last year, following adoption of the FY 2009-10 Budget, the City Council reviewed the annual
Work Program for the City of Palos Verdes Estates. The purpose of the Work Program is to
identify work milestones and projected target dates as part of an overall strategy to manage the
workload of each of the Departments. The Work Program subsequently was reviewed and updated
on January 13, 2010.

This report presents the FY 2010-11Work Program for major work activities occurring over the
next 12 months. As previously indicated, while the Work Program captures many of the
departments’ work activities, it is not a complete list of all our duties and responsibilities. The
Work Program is intended to highlight some of the more notable work projects and/or items that are
new for the coming year, or in some instances, carried forward from the prior year.

In terms of the FY 2010-11 Work Program, I would like to highlight a few projects and activities as
described below:

  In the City Manager’s Office, major work activities will include the establishment of an
  emissions reduction goal as related to our municipal operations to be followed by
  development of a Local Climate Action Plan to achieve the targeted reduction. Similar work
  will occur as related to greenhouse gas emissions and energy usage on a citywide basis. In
  the area of human resources, we will complete a number of tasks including (1) Completion
  of harassment and discrimination prevention training through the California Joint Powers
  Insurance Authority (CJPIA); (2) Preparation of an RFP for health insurance broker
  services; (3) Update of the City’s Personnel Regulations as initiated in FY 2009-10; and (4)
  Completion of labor discussions with PVE’s employee groups. Lastly, we will also work
  with the CJPIA and Departments to undertake a comprehensive review and update of our
  employee safety programs in the coming year.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
JULY 13, 2010
  23
   The Work Program for the City Clerk/Finance Department includes the completion of the
  City’s new web page which will go live August 1, 2010. The Work Program anticipates the
  expiration of the Cox Television Franchise in October 2010 and the transition of cable
  regulations to a State Franchise pursuant to State law. Council will note that milestones are
  included in the City Clerk’s Work Program in preparation of the City Council election of
  March 8, 2011. The comprehensive review of the PVE Municipal Code is a carry-over item
  from prior year Work Programs and will be completed in FY 2010-11 with the involvement
  of the City Attorney’s office and operating departments. Lastly, the Finance Department
  will issue an RFP for audit services and once again undertake a review of the City’s existing
  pension obligations and evaluate the feasibility of an additional lump sum contribution to
  PERS to reduce PVE’s existing pension liabilities.

  In the Planning and Public Works Department, the most significant projects will be the
  replacement of the Via Barri and the Rocky Point Road underground sewage pump stations.
  These pump stations are nearing the end of their useful life and failure of either station
  would cause significant hardship to our residents, as well as severe financial consequences

  Planning/Public Works projects in 2010-11 include the seismic study of City Hall, an update

  The Police Department Work Program includes milestones for study/replacement of the

The Work Program is organized by Department and includes a summary table of the City’s Capital

As unforeseen events occur throughout the year, circumstances may affect the priority of projects
and/or new unanticipated projects may be added as necessary. We will bring the Work Program to
the City Council in January 2011 with updates and changes as become necessary.

NEW BUSINESS

REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF THE PALOS VERDES STABLE FY 2010-11 OPERATING
BUDGET

City Manager Hoefgen reported that the HGS Incorporated has now operated the Stables since March
of 2009. The first year was a transition period with many things changing at the Stables such as
additional boarders coming to the Stables and other boarders leaving the Stables. The revenues for
2009-10 were $488,000 and expenditures were just over $418,000 with a net profit of about $70,000.
For 2010-11 there are no proposed changes for the monthly boarding or service fees. The Stables are
at full capacity and for the coming year the boarding revenue should be $420,000 and training fees
revenue should be $60,000. HGS Management is focused on developing new revenue streams. The
largest single cost of operating the Stables is staffing at $175,000. The cost of hay has been reduced
from the original budget projections due to instituting the premium charges for the more expensive
hay. The budget allocates significant resources, $24,000, for upkeep and maintenance of the facility.
For FY 2010-11, the net profit is projected at $83,190 which reflects payment of the 5% concession fee
to the City totaling $25,000. The Council Liaisons Mayor Pro Tem Rea and Council member Perkins
along with City Manager Hoefgen met with David McLewee and Erin Isom-McLewee to review all
the information which is included in the staff report.

Councilmember Bird said, with respect to the 2009-10 budget, hay cost less than was budgeted for and
he wondered why the 2010-11 budget for hay is even higher. City Manager Hoefgen said the budget
reflects the current higher cost of hay and also reflects the Stables being at full capacity now.
Councilmember Bird congratulated the concessionaire on running the Stables at a profit and doing a
good job providing the Stables services to residents.

CITY COUNCIL  2
JULY 13, 2010
 Mayor Pro Tem Rea commented that this is his first time as a Stable Liaison and he is impressed at the
McLewee’s ability to turn the Stables into a profitable operation which is generating a concession fee
to the City.

Councilmember Perkins also is pleased with the progress the McLewees have made in just one year.
She was also originally concerned with the cost of hay and shavings, but she was reassured during the
Liaison meeting that the difference was due to boarders not opting to purchase the premium hay. She
was concerned about the issue of availability of Western riding lessons and was told there is a Western
trainer available but the demand is not high. Another issue that had been previously raised was the
amount of ring time Erin Isom-McLewee was using as allowed in the Concession Agreement.
Councilmember Perkins is confident that Erin is well below the use that is permitted. She said the
McLewees are to be complimented on the marvelous job they are doing with the Stables.

Councilmember Goodhart is also pleased that the Stables are doing so well. The initial issues have
been settled. He believes the Stables are now being run like a business and he likes that the McLewees
are planning for capital improvements in the upcoming year. He is happy to see trail rides return to the
Stables.

Mayor Humphrey said the McLewees are to be commended.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said the expenses were higher than budgeted, but so was the revenue. The bottom
line ended up close to the projections despite all the uncertainties.

Erin Isom-McLewee, manager/concessionaire of the Stables, said she used to go to the PV Stables as a
child and remembered it being full of life with the trail rides, riding schools, and kids everywhere. She
said when they took over as the concessionaire much of that was gone but now it is back to how it used
to be with a lot of kids, camps, people watching their kids take lessons – it is an alive, happy place.

Mayor Humphrey thanked the McLewees for a job well done.

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea, seconded by Councilmember Perkins, and unanimously
approved by a roll call vote to approve the FY 2010-11 Palos Verdes Stable Operating Budget.

STATUS REPORT ON EFFORTS TO DEVELOP A DOG PARK ON A PORTION OF THE
FORMER PALOS VERDES LANDFILL PROPERTY

City Manager Hoefgen said the site of the former Palos Verdes Landfill has been a subject of great
interest to those seeking a location for a dog park. The land is owned by Los Angeles County and is
located in Rolling Hills Estates. The property is 175 acres of which 1-2 acres have been proposed for
use as a fenced park area for owners and their dogs. The City Council of Rolling Hills Estates has
written a letter to Supervisor Knabe in support of locating a dog park at the site. The effort to develop
a location for a dog park has been lead by Palos Verdes Estates residents Bruce and Maureen
Megowan. He noted that this item is not a request for financial support for the dog park.

CITY COUNCIL  3
JULY 13, 2010
 Mayor Humphrey had spoken with the Megowans and they were hopeful the Council would send a
letter of support. She reiterated that Palos Verdes Estates does not usually get involved with telling
another City what to do with their property, but in this instance the City of Rolling Hills Estates (RHE)
has already taken a position of support and would welcome the support of PVE.

Councilmember Goodhart asked if there was any discussion at the RHE council meeting about how the
costs would be covered. City Manager Hoefgen said his understanding is that it would be through
contributions and private fundraising.

Councilmember Perkins asked if RHE had solicited PVE’s support or was this PVE’s idea. Mayor
Humphrey responded that community members asked PVE to send a letter of support.
Councilmember Perkins appreciated the language of the support letter clarifying that PVE is not
wishing to interfere with a land use decision, but rather to express support of the use of a portion of the
site for a dog park in support of RHE.

Councilmember Goodhart agreed that he liked the language of the letter. He also thanked the
Megowans for taking on this ‘labor of love’.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea has also been interested in the possibility of a dog park in PVE and he knows staff
has determined that there is no suitable area within PVE to locate a dog park. He understands that the
boundaries of the landfill are located within RHE, but the land belongs to the County which is why
PVE would direct the letter to the County.

Councilmember Goodhart moved, it was seconded by Councilmember Bird, and unanimously
approved to send a letter to Los Angeles County 4th District Supervisor Knabe’s office in support of the
development of a dog park on a portion of the former Palos Verdes landfill property.

PALOS VERDES ESTATES MUNICIPAL CODE REVIEW AND RECODIFICATION

Assistant City Manager Smith reported that the last comprehensive update of the Municipal Code was
in 1988. There has been some progress in this project to date including a review by the Code
Publishing Company which produced a legal review analysis that will be helpful to the City Attorney
and staff. The bulk of the project will be accomplished in the next 12 months. In order to proceed in
an orderly and timely fashion, staff wanted to take the first step in providing this report that outlines the
parameters for the review. The intent is to update the Code, including statutory references, to eliminate
any vague, ambiguous or overly broad language, correct and update Code provisions that are
inconsistent with current practice and to correct internal inconsistencies in the Code. It is not the intent
of the project to review and revise policies under which the City currently operates.

Mayor Humphrey had questions regarding the time-line and wondered if it was ambitious. Assistant
City Manager Smith said the time-line outlined is an educated guess at this point and she assured the
Mayor that the project would not be rushed.

Councilmember Goodhart said that the School Board had undertaken a similar task years ago and a
firm was hired to handle the project – he wondered if staff was going to handle what could turn into a
significant task or is a subcontractor going to do the work. Assistant City Manager Smith said that
CITY COUNCIL  4
JULY 13, 2010
 subject has not be broached yet, but it may be better to have the City Attorney work with staff as they
are the ones that represent the City and help staff maneuver through the Municipal Code.
Councilmember Goodhart said he just wanted to make sure that whoever handles the task, that it will
be handled efficiently and effectively.

Councilmember Perkins said she had the same question regarding who will be handling the project.
She believes that as the time-line is created, she would want enough time for the Council to go through
the chapters and ask questions. She realizes that updating the Code will prompt conversations on
current policies and practices.

Mayor Humphrey envisions the entire Municipal Code being given to Council in a red-line version.
City Attorney Hogin said she envisions presenting the Code to Council a chapter or two at a time to
keep it palatable.

Councilmember Perkins asked if the sections that pertain to zoning must go to the Planning
Commission for review. City Attorney Hogin responded that when the Council actually implements
the ordinances that make the changes, there will be a longer process that will involve the Planning
Commission. She and Assistant City Manager Smith would like to give the Council a sort of preview
prior to holding the actual public hearings.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked if the process would take place in Open Session. City Attorney Hogin said
it would take place in Open Session and if it is too much of a burden for the regular Council agenda
then the Council may want to consider having workshops.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked about the money that had been budgeted for the Code revision for payment
to an outside vendor. Assistant City Manager Smith said that was for the first blush legal review of the
Code for statutory mandates and vague and ambiguous language and has already been completed.

Councilmember Bird said he would prefer to set aside a few Saturdays to go through the Code instead
of a chapter or two at a time during a regular Council meeting.

The Council agreed with the objectives set forth in the staff report: 1) update the Code, including
statutory references, to reflect current state and federal law; 2) eliminate vague, ambiguous and overly
broad language; 3) Correct/update provisions which are inconsistent with current practice; and 4)
correct internal inconsistencies within the Code. The Council would also like the City Attorney to
incorporate best practices from other agencies for consideration by Council as part of the update of the
Municipal Code.

City Manager’s Report – Presentation of FY 2010-11 Work Program

City Manager Hoefgen reported that the Work Program highlights major work activities and
projects for the upcoming year. He highlighted a few items from each Department. In the City
Manager’s office one of the major priorities is the Green Program which will establish an emissions
CITY COUNCIL  5

 reduction target as well as a Climate Action Plan to achieve that target. There are a number of
Human Resources programs and activities – Labor negotiations, RFP for insurance broker services,
and a review of the safety plan programs working with the Joint Powers Insurance Association.
Also, there is the ongoing work with the City concessions. In the City Clerk and Finance
Departments the website redesign should be complete by August 1st, there is an election in March
2011, the Municipal Code update, the budget process, the RFP for audit services, a review of
pension obligations, and the implementation of the State franchise agreement for cable services. In
the Police Department there are a number of significant projects and programs with the
implementation of the Disaster District Plan, promotions for Captain and other personnel,
replacement of radio system, updates to the Policy Manual, and continuation of the PVE CARES

pump stations being replaced, the slurry and overlay programs, the seismic analysis of City Hall, an
update to the Pavement Management Program, and the continued monitoring of the Malaga Cove
groundwater.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked who is required to take AB1234 training. City Attorney Hogin
responded that training is legally required every two years by anyone who receives compensation or
reimbursement.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked about the 401A program. City Manager Hoefgen said the program is a
way for employees to take leave balances that are available for cash-out to be able to roll these into
a deferred compensation type benefit.

Councilmember Goodhart asked about the state mandate to provide low cost housing and how the
City plans to deal with the requirement. City Manager Hoefgen said the plan is not specifically
enumerated in the Work Program, but there are on-going programs that the City has in place in the
Planning and Public Works Department.

Councilmember Goodhart said the issue of the management of the City owned homes had not been
discussed in awhile and wondered how and when the City plans to deal with this. City Manager
Hoefgen responded that the most immediate issue is the soon to be vacant City home which has
been scheduled to be discussed with the Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem. Mayor Humphrey said she
plans to have it on an upcoming agenda.

The City Council received the report and the Mayor thanked staff for their work in putting the Work
